title: rationalize-weight-manifest-and-streaming-loader-interchange
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Consolidate and modernize the model weight manifest and the streaming weight loader interchange so that different checkpoint formats (sharded, monolithic, delta-weights) can be uniformly discovered, streamed, and validated. Reduce cold-start load time variance, simplify downstream tokenizer adapter logic, and establish a forward-compatible manifest v2 that supports partial-shard ranges and progressive verification.
acceptance_criteria: Introduce manifest v2 specification that describes shard ranges, checksum per chunk, optional compression metadata, and tokenizer binding info
Streaming loader supports manifest v1 and v2: falls back to v1 legacy path when manifest v2 is absent
Cold-start model load (from empty service cache) median time reduced by >=20% for typical 8-shard checkpoints in internal perf tests
Tokenizer adaptor consumes manifest metadata instead of custom sidecar files; tokenizer init sequence reduced to single RPC and deterministic ordering
Unit and integration tests cover progressive chunk validation, partial-shard resume, and intentional corruption detection with clear error codes
Migration plan documented and tested: can toggle manifest-v2-on by model tag and rollback without restart
tasks: Draft manifest v2 spec (schema + plain-language examples) and circulate to runtime, model-ingest, and QA
Implement manifest v2 producer in model-upload service (s3/gs metadata generation) with toggle flag
Add streaming loader runtime support for chunked shard download + per-chunk checksum verification
Refactor tokenizer adaptor to read tokenizer binding and vocab offsets from manifest instead of sidecar
Benchmark cold-start and steady-state loading across a representative matrix of checkpoints (1, 4, 8, 16 shards; compressed vs uncompressed)
Add end-to-end integration test harness that simulates partial shard availability and resume behavior
Create rollout plan: feature flag per-model, gradual enable in staging, canary 5% prod, full enable
Document migration steps for partners who upload legacy-format checkpoints
comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Patel: Initial triage — observed large variance in cold-start times when upstream storage returns shards at inconsistent latencies. Proposed unified manifest to give runtime precise per-chunk expectations.

2026-02-24 Marco Li: Spike complete. Proof-of-concept streaming consumer reduces first-token latency by ~18% in our single-run profile (8-shard Llama2-70b test). Raised concern about storage cost if we add per-chunk checksums; suggested using small 64-bit checksums (xxhash64) only for compressed shards.

2026-02-28 Design review (Runtime team): prefer schema-first approach. Action: publish manifest v2 JSON Schema and OpenAPI examples. Link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INGEST/Manifest+v2+Spec
2026-03-03 UX/Console note (from Priya Rao): Console ingest UI should show manifest version and per-shard health. Created follow-up ticket PM-4572 for small console changes.

2026-03-08 Marco Li: Implemented streaming loader prototype with per-chunk validation. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1428 — awaiting review. Unit tests added for resume behavior.

2026-03-10 QA (Jorge Mendes): Integration tests show two edge cases: (1) upstream returns chunk order out-of-sequence — handled by buffering but increases memory; (2) corrupted chunk triggers full-shard fallback which is expensive. Decision: add prioritized retry (N=2) using same-storage-region endpoint before fallback to full-shard re-download.
2026-03-12 Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include progressive verification and migration toggle. Next: finalize schema and land producer changes in upload service.
